source.title: 2025 IC3 Complainants 17 Years Old or Younger Annual Report, by state
source.license: Work of the United States Government; not subject to copyright in the United States.

note: One row per state page, as published. 'victims' are counted by the state of the victim and 'subjects' by the state of the person complained about; only crime types and descriptors with a non-zero count or loss are kept. Descriptors (crimes_against_children, ai_related, cryptocurrency, cryptocurrency_wallet) are tags on top of a crime type, so they overlap with the crime types.
caveats: These pages do not match the state table in the annual report PDF (pp.37-38), which counts every complaint filed by someone 17 or younger: for example Alabama has 175 complaints in the PDF and 122 victims here. The pages appear to cover complaints tagged Crimes Against Children, which an adult can file on a child's behalf, which is why the age table includes adults. IC3 does not explain the difference, so the two sources are stored separately and never added together.
Almost all victims are filed under Extortion or Other. For children, extortion in IC3 data is mostly sextortion.
Reported complaints only: a floor, not a measure of how many children were targeted.
